title: Network pharmacology-guided self-assembling quercetin hydrogel from Astragalus membranaceous accelerates diabetic wound healing.
authors: Liu, Meixuan; Zhou, Hanlei; Wang, Jialiang; Wang, Yiran; Cai, Chenghao; Han, Chunmao; Dong, Lina; Wang, Xingang
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究黄芪中槲皮素水凝胶促进糖尿病创面愈合，涉及网络药理学和分子对接，但核心是药物递送与伤口修复，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系或结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Delayed diabetic wound healing remains a significant clinical challenge. Astragalus membranaceus, a traditional Chinese herb, is widely used for the topical treatment of diabetic wounds. However, its complex composition has hampered the identification of its main active components and precise mechanisms of action. PURPOSE: This study aimed to identify the main active component of A. membranaceous responsible for diabetic wound healing and to develop an advanced nanocomposite delivery system to enhance its therapeutic efficacy. METHODS: The main active component and its core therapeutic targets were screened using network pharmacology and validated by molecular docking. To address the inherent limitations of the identified component, quercetin-loaded chitosan nanoparticles (QNPs) were fabricated via self-assembly and subsequently incorporated into a gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA) hydrogel to form QNPs@GelMA. The therapeutic effects of QNPs@GelMA were systematically evaluated in vitro and in vivo using a range of techniques including ROS test, histopathological staining, immunofluorescence, and TUNEL staining. RESULTS: Network pharmacology and molecular docking identified quercetin as the main active component of A. membranaceous, with core targets involving JUN, IL-6, IL-1beta, and TP53. The constructed QNPs@GelMA hydrogel facilitated sustained release of quercetin at the wound site. In cellular and animal experiments, QNPs@GelMA significantly enhanced diabetic wound healing by exerting potent antioxidative and anti-inflammatory effects, promoting macrophage M2 polarization, stimulating angiogenesis, and inhibiting apoptosis. Mechanistically, the hydrogel downregulated the protein expression of RAGE and NF-kappaB. CONCLUSION: This study elucidated that quercetin was the main active component of A. membranaceous for diabetic wound healing. The QNPs@GelMA hydrogel exhibited excellent wound repair properties via downregulating RAGE/NF-kappaB signaling pathway, offering an advanced dressing for the treatment of diabetic wounds and providing a novel methodology for identifying active components in traditional herbs.
abstract_zh: 背景：糖尿病创面愈合延迟仍是临床上的重大挑战。黄芪（Astragalus membranaceus）作为一种传统中草药，广泛用于糖尿病创面的局部治疗。然而，其复杂成分阻碍了主要活性成分及精确作用机制的鉴定。目的：本研究旨在鉴定黄芪中促进糖尿病创面愈合的主要活性成分，并开发一种先进的纳米复合递送系统以增强其治疗效果。方法：通过网络药理学筛选主要活性成分及其核心治疗靶点，并通过分子对接 (molecular docking) 验证。为解决所鉴定成分的固有局限性，通过自组装制备了槲皮素负载壳聚糖纳米颗粒 (quercetin-loaded chitosan nanoparticles, QNPs)，随后将其掺入甲基丙烯酰化明胶 (gelatin methacryloyl, GelMA) 水凝胶中，形成QNPs@GelMA。通过一系列技术，包括ROS检测、组织病理学染色、免疫荧光和TUNEL染色，在体外和体内系统评估了QNPs@GelMA的治疗效果。结果：网络药理学和分子对接鉴定槲皮素为黄芪的主要活性成分，核心靶点涉及JUN、IL-6、IL-1beta和TP53。构建的QNPs@GelMA水凝胶在创面部位实现槲皮素的持续释放。在细胞和动物实验中，QNPs@GelMA通过发挥强效抗氧化和抗炎作用、促进巨噬细胞M2极化、刺激血管生成及抑制凋亡，显著增强糖尿病创面愈合。机制上，该水凝胶下调了RAGE和NF-kappaB的蛋白表达。结论：本研究阐明槲皮素是黄芪中促进糖尿病创面愈合的主要活性成分。QNPs@GelMA水凝胶通过下调RAGE/NF-kappaB信号通路表现出优异的创面修复性能，为糖尿病创面治疗提供了一种先进敷料，并为鉴定传统草药中的活性成分提供了一种新方法。
